milestone: BranchWrite local FIFO recovery after client process death
verified: A new user message is atomically stored in the private local queue while a previous COW request is active.
The client OS process is killed after COW accepts its operation.
COW finishes the earlier answer after the client has died.
The queued process cannot send while the chat state still has an unresolved operation.
A new BranchWrite process reconciles the original operation ID, then drains the queued message.
COW history contains both user messages in FIFO order and both original operation IDs exactly once.
limitations: Uses real BranchWrite subprocesses and COW coordinator/Store/HTTP handler with deterministic synthetic CPU FlowModel.
The queue-specific test leaves the COW service process alive; separate process restart coverage is in validation/cow-http-process-restart-20261020/.
No real GPU inference, native KV restore, disk-full or power-loss test.
